Switzerland To Vote On Ending Fractional Reserve Banking

This was posted previously from a different source. In the other topic most people had no idea that banks are not only allowed to but actually do create the vast majority of money today. In fact only a tiny fraction of all money is actually created by the government - around 3% in fact.

So how do private banks create money? Fractional reserve lending. Fractional reserve is far more insidious than it seems at first. What a fractional reserve means is that banks only need to hold a fraction of what they lend out - 10% in most countries including the US. So how does this create money?

  • I go deposit $100 at Bank America.
  • They now lend out $90 and keep $10 on hand. If I wanted my $100 back, they wouldn't have it. This is legal and where the central bank would come save the day.
  • That $90 gets spent and deposited at another bank, if not the same one. This bank now keeps $9 on hand and lends out $81.
  • This process continues onward until there's no money left.

In the end my real money deposit of $100 will end up creating $1000 of new money that's created in the form of debt and put into circulation. This is how nearly all new money is created. The government themselves print only a tiny fraction of all new money that enters into the system. This is also a very dangerous game as most of all new money being created in the form of debt has enormous implications, but let's keep it simple for now!

As I posted in the other topic, fractional reserve banking is a myth. Money is created as credit based on the capital reserves of the bank, not the cash in its vaults. They never need the cash until a customer needs to do a non-electronic transfer, at which point the bank could effectively just print the cash and destroy it when it gets re-deposited by whoever gets paid by the customer.

This is not theoretical, it is the result of analysis of how banking actually works. Bing "Modern Monetary Theory" for more.

This widespread misunderstanding is a good reason why referenda and direct democracy are a dumb idea. Low information voters can do a lot of damage.

Whether the money is electronic or physical obviously makes no difference. The point is that fractional reserve banking results in a large multiplication of money based on any given input. And this multiplication is the source of nearly all "new" money in the economy today.
